Put the tagging right: figures in the wrong unit, signs the wrong way

Source: R/xbrl_standardise.R
xbrl_standardise.Rd

A filing tags each figure in kroner, and now and then a line is tagged in thousands instead – most often in the comparative column, so that last year's land and buildings of 2,981,848 reappears this year as 2,982. That is a technicality of the tagging, not a fact about the company, and left in place it reads as the company's accounts changing by a factor of a thousand. This finds such figures between filings and puts them back.

Usage

xbrl_standardise(x, what = c("units", "signs"), tol = 1)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl(). For units, several years of at least some companies. A company with one filing has no units to compare and keeps its figures.

what

Which to standardise: "units", "signs", or both, the default. Units go first, because a figure in the wrong unit would make a statement fail to add up for a reason of its own.

tol

Absolute tolerance, in the reporting currency, for whether an activity adds up. Default 1.

Value

x, with value corrected where a figure was in the wrong unit or had its sign reversed, and the columns value_tagged and standardised added. Attribute "standardisation" is a tibble with one row per figure looked at: kind ("unit" or "sign"), the filing, the company, the element, the date, the figure as tagged and as standardised, action ("corrected comparative", "flipped sign" or "undecided") and detail.

Which figure is the wrong one

A figure stated in two filings that disagree by a power of a thousand has two candidates for the mistake. A third figure can decide: the later filing's own figure for the same line in its own year. If it is of the earlier filing's order, the later filing disagrees with itself – its comparative column is in a different unit from its own year – and that is proof enough. The comparative is corrected.

The opposite case is not settled. When the later filing's two columns agree and the earlier filing is the odd one, the earlier filing may be wrong, or the later filing may be tagged in thousands throughout. The two look the same from here. The figure is listed as undecided and left as it is.

Over 4,304 filings for 2020-2024, 147 figures were corrected and 49 left undecided. A filing with a corrected comparative typically had three lines affected, about a sixth of its comparable balances: a column tagged in the wrong unit, not a company reporting in thousands.

What changes

The figure is multiplied or divided by the power of a thousand that brings it into line, so its own digits are kept and only the unit moves. Every copy of the fact moves with it: the same element, filing, date and basis. value_tagged keeps the figure as tagged and standardised says why it moved, on every row that did; elsewhere they are the value and NA. Nothing else in the filing is touched.

Signs in the cash flow statement

A line in investing or financing whose activity does not add up as tagged, and does add up with that one line reversed, has its sign reversed. The statement itself says which way the filer meant it. The same test is made one level up, of the three activities against the change in cash.

What is not touched is as important. A line whose activity adds up as tagged keeps its sign, however its sign looks beside its element, because then the sign means something. A sale of a company reported negative in an investing activity that adds up with it – Greenland Airports' grant taken to income, in its 2025 group accounts – is a misclassification for the screen to find, not a sign to correct. Where several lines would each make the activity add up, none is reversed and the case is listed as undecided. Operating is left alone, because its lines are the income statement's own facts.

See also

check_continuity(), which finds these figures, and xbrl_screen(), which standardises before it screens.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
x <- xbrl_standardise(x)
attr(x, "standardisation")
x[!is.na(x$standardised), c("cvr", "elementid", "value_tagged", "value")]
} # }
